newsitem.title: GERMANY: Ex-Stasi officers on trial for aiding guerrillas.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Stasi officers on trial for aiding guerrillas.

text.p: Four former East German intelligence officers went on trial in Berlin on Wednesday charged with helping some of West Germany's most wanted guerrillas start new lives and escape justice in the West.

Harry Dahl, 67, head of the counter-terrorism deparment at East Berlin's Ministry for State Security (Stasi) and three of his top officers, Guenter Jaeckel, 62, Hans-Hermann Petzold, 52, and Gerd Zaumseil, 48, stand accused of preventing justice.

The case is the latest to try to determine how far East Berlin supported international terrorism and punish those behind an "unholy alliance" between the Stasi and the leftist Red Army Faction (RAF), that struck fear into the West German establishment during the 1970s and 1980s.

Prosecutors say the four accused were responsible for letting the guerrillas enter the former Soviet satellite state, giving them new identities, money to settle in, finding them flats and work from the early 1980s until 1990.
Defence lawyers in the case say their clients do not dispute having helped the RAF members settle in East Germany but they deny preventing the course of justice.
They argue the officers prevented attacks in then-West Germany because the guerrillas were taken out of circulation and helped to lead a "peaceful existence" for a decade.

They also argue their clients had been acting on the direct orders of then powerful Stasi chief Erich Mielke and that this "counter-terrorist" mission had the blessing of East Germany's last hardline ruler, Erich Honecker.
